title: DFARS and Domestic Metals: A Complete Guide for Defense Contractors
summary: Separate material specifications, specialty-metal clauses, domestic-origin requirements and supplier documentation when purchasing metal for a defense order.
body_markdown:
## Identify the material before applying the clause


DFARS 252.225-7009 defines specialty metal using specific categories: certain steels, certain nickel or iron-nickel and cobalt alloys, titanium and its alloys, and zirconium and its alloys. Ordinary aluminum plate is outside that definition. The mention of aluminum as an alloying element in steel does not make aluminum plate a specialty metal.


[DFARS 7009: scope and rules](https://www.acquisition.gov/dfars/252.225-7009-restriction-acquisition-certain-articles-containing-specialty-metals.)


## Separate the sourcing questions


For covered specialty metals, paragraph (b) of 252.225-7009 addresses where the metal is melted or produced, subject to the clause’s exceptions. It is not a universal rule that all aluminum must be melted and manufactured in qualifying countries. Other clauses and purchase-order terms can establish their own requirements. Review the clause actually included in the order, including its revision and scope.


[DFARS 7009: scope and rules](https://www.acquisition.gov/dfars/252.225-7009-restriction-acquisition-certain-articles-containing-specialty-metals.)[DFARS 7014: reserved](https://www.acquisition.gov/dfars/252.225-7014-reserved.)


## Use the applicable country definition


A domestic-melt requirement and a qualifying-country requirement are not interchangeable. Use the definition referenced by the applicable clause; an old country list copied into a supplier article can become stale. Buying from a United States distributor does not itself prove where the material was produced.


[DFARS 225.003: countries](https://www.acquisition.gov/dfars/225.003-definitions.)


## Build an order-specific documentation package


Read the actual certificate package against the order. An MTR may include origin information, or the supplier may provide additional source documentation. A document title, mill address or distributor address alone does not establish every required fact. Match the supplied heat or lot to the records and resolve missing information before acceptance.


Requirement Record to confirm


Alloy, temper and material specification Actual supplied heat or lot and its mill certificate


Required melt, smelt or manufacture origin The corresponding source declaration and traceability


Approved supplier or quality-system requirement The approval or certificate required by the order


Record retention and submission format The customer’s stated duration, format and delivery requirement


## Resolve unclear terms before accepting a substitution


If a flow-down does not clearly identify what applies to an aluminum item, obtain clarification from the buyer or contracts team. Do not infer an exemption from a commercial-item label, a price threshold or the absence of one clause. For a substitution, confirm both the engineering approval and any sourcing requirements.


[How to read a mill certificate](https://noxmetals.co/blog/how-to-read-mill-cert)[Origin and mill certificates](https://noxmetals.co/services/dfars-compliance)[Shop 7050 aluminum plate](https://noxmetals.co/materials/7050-aluminum)
